---
title: "Lucid"
subtitle: "A clear, accessible theme for teaching and technical writing"
description: "Principles, installation, options, customisation, and base typography."
---

Lucid is a Quarto format for material that people study rather than skim: textbooks, course sites, lab manuals, and technical reports. It favours legible type, a palette that stays distinguishable for colour-blind readers, restrained geometry, and interactions that work from a keyboard.

## Principles

Clarity first
: Prose sits at a measure of 76 characters. Headings use Jost, body text uses Libre Franklin, and numbers in tables share one width so columns line up.

Colour that works for every reader
: Accents come from the viridis scale, which stays perceptually even and distinguishable under common colour-vision deficiencies. Neutrals are charcoal and paper.

Restrained geometry
: Corners are nearly square. A component gets one hairline frame and one coloured edge, never a heavy shadow.

Accessible by default
: Table headers carry `scope`, wide tables become focusable scroll regions, collapsible callouts respond to Enter and Space, and diagrams receive an SVG title and description.

Faithful on paper
: Print styles switch to black on white, hide navigation, and keep tables, pseudocode, and diagrams legible.

## Install and use

```bash
quarto add brenobeirigo/quarto-themes
```

```yaml
format:
  lucid-html: default
```

Any ordinary HTML option still works under `lucid-html`. For a book, also set `reader-mode: true` under `book:` to enable the wide reading layout.

## Options

Each enhancement can be switched off under `lucid:` in document or project metadata.

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `accessible-tables` | `true` | Adds `scope` to header cells and turns the first column of `.row-headers` tables into row headers |
| `pseudocode` | `true` | Renders `.pseudocode` code blocks as a numbered terminal |
| `flowcharts` | `true` | Keeps Mermaid diagrams at a readable size and adds an SVG title and description |
| `callouts` | `true` | Makes collapsible callouts keyboard-operable and retitles solution callouts |
| `copy-refs` | `true` | Adds a copy-reference button to numbered labels in headings |
| `table-scroll` | `true` | Makes wide tables focusable scroll regions with a hint on small screens |
| `page-references` | `false` | Keeps the page-local bibliography visible on every citing page |

: Options read by the Lucid filter {#tbl-lucid-options .data-table}

```yaml
lucid:
  copy-refs: false
  page-references: true
```

## Customise

### Colours and fonts

Every token in `lucid-light.scss` and `lucid-dark.scss` is a `!default` Sass variable. Put your values in a brand file and list it after the palette. Listing a theme replaces the one the format supplies, so name the Lucid layers too.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$lucid-accent: #2a9d8f;
$lucid-accent-strong: #1d6f65;
$lucid-font-heading: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif;
```

```yaml
format:
  lucid-html:
    theme:
      light:
        - cosmo
        - _extensions/brenobeirigo/lucid/scss/lucid.scss
        - _extensions/brenobeirigo/lucid/scss/lucid-light.scss
        - brand.scss
      dark:
        - darkly
        - _extensions/brenobeirigo/lucid/scss/lucid.scss
        - _extensions/brenobeirigo/lucid/scss/lucid-dark.scss
        - brand.scss
```

### One component

Components read CSS custom properties, so a small stylesheet can adjust them without recompiling the theme.

```css
.landing-page {
  --lucid-accent-light: #ffd166;
}
```

## Typography

### A third-level heading

Body text carries **strong emphasis**, *emphasis*, `inline code`, and [a link](components.qmd). Footnotes appear in the margin or at the end of the page.^[Footnotes use the body typeface at a smaller size.]

> A block quotation keeps the reading measure and sets itself apart with a rule.

#### A fourth-level heading

1. Ordered lists keep their numbers aligned.
2. Nested content stays within the measure.
   - Unordered items use the body colour.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
A note uses the viridis blue edge.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
A tip uses the strong green edge.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
A warning uses the light green edge.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Important and caution callouts use the ink colour.
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## A collapsed callout

Focus the header and press Enter or Space to open it.
:::

## Code

```python
def running_total(values):
    """Return the cumulative sum after each value."""
    total = 0
    totals = []
    for value in values:
        total += value
        totals.append(total)
    return totals
```
